title: Cost an electric bus over its life

blocks.text: A city transit agency (invented for this practice) compares bus purchases by lifecycle cost. A bus has a price paid now, a running cost (energy and maintenance) paid at the end of each year of its life, some one-off costs in given years of its life (a battery replacement, say, in year 6), and a resale value received at the end of its life. Everything is in $k of today's prices, and the agency's real rate is `rate`.
Write `lifecycle_cost(price, running, life, rate, one_offs, resale)`, the bus's lifecycle cost on today's date. `one_offs` is `{year of life: cost}`, with years counted from 1.
Write the lifecycle cost as one formula first, with each of its four terms. About six lines.

print("price 700, running 45, 10 years, 0%, no extras:", round(lifecycle_cost(700, 45, 10, 0.0, {}, 0), 2))
print("same at 4%:", round(lifecycle_cost(700, 45, 10, 0.04, {}, 0), 2))
print("at 4%, overhaul 120 in year 5, resale 80:",
      round(lifecycle_cost(700, 45, 10, 0.04, {5: 120}, 80), 2))

cases.says: at a zero rate the lifecycle cost is the price, every year's running cost, the one-off costs, less the resale value
the first year's running cost is discounted one year, and the last is paid at the end of the life
a battery replacement in year six of the life is discounted six years
the resale value received at the end of the life reduces the cost by its present value, not its face value
